components.text: Whether theism better explains genuine human freedom than materialism does.
The earlier move requires an account of why rationality, mathematics, and freedom favor an originating mind over materialism.
The claim that theism supports genuine freedom and responsibility better than materialism.
The claim that divine grounding secures objective morality rather than threatening moral autonomy.
The earlier move's decisive demand is whether objective moral obligation requires grounding in God's nature and a moral lawgiver.
The earlier move also claims that genuine human freedom is difficult to ground on materialism.
Whether a cosmic beginning warrants the asserted supernatural personal cause.
Whether design evidence establishes a creator rather than merely proposing one.
Whether biological information warrants an intelligent divine source.
The earlier move must justify the inference from the universe's beginning to a supernatural personal cause rather than merely assert it.
The earlier design move must show that life-permitting conditions comparatively warrant intelligent agency.
The earlier biological move must show why DNA information warrants an intelligent source over natural mechanisms.
Whether evidence for design establishes the specifically intervening and Christian God.
Whether an intelligent source for life establishes Christian miracles and authority.
Whether a cosmic personal cause establishes an interventionist Christian deity.
The earlier design inference establishes at most an intelligent designer unless a further bridge to intervening Christian claims is supplied.
The biological design inference likewise requires a separate route from intelligent source to Christianity.
A personal cosmic cause still requires evidence for prayer, incarnation, resurrection, and redemption.
Whether objective moral obligation requires grounding in God's nature and a lawgiver.
Whether atheists can know moral truths or perform moral actions without belief in God.
The earlier move asks what ontologically grounds objective moral obligation, not whether atheists can know morality or behave well.
Whether religious wrongdoing determines God's existence or rebuts the offered existence evidence.
Whether the opening evidence establishes Christianity rather than only generic theism.
Whether the proposed creator is merely one unsupported deity among many.
The earlier move combines behavioral claims about religion with an implied consequence for whether the offered evidence establishes God's existence.
The earlier move requires separating generic design evidence from distinctive Christian conclusions.
The earlier move requires justification for selecting the relevant conception of deity.
Whether biological complexity requires intelligence rather than mutation and natural selection.
Whether unexplained order licenses inference to a supervising designer.
The earlier move claims DNA complexity cannot arise through unguided natural laws and therefore indicates intelligent agency.
The earlier move attributes natural complexity and life-permitting order to a designer.
Whether lack of a natural predecessor entails a supernatural personal author.
Whether the affirmative has supplied evidence sufficient for its generic creator attributes.
The earlier move infers a supernatural personal author from the beginning of space, time, matter, and the absence of a natural antecedent.
Whether generic creator evidence can be separated from objections to specific Christian doctrines.
The earlier move distinguishes generic creator evidence from Christianity and separates believers' wrongdoing from the existence question.
Whether DNA complexity by itself warrants inference to an intelligent divine source.
Whether the prior generic-theism evidence establishes its claimed creator conclusion.
The earlier move claims DNA information positively indicates intelligence and excludes an origin solely through unguided natural laws.
The demand for separate evidence connecting generic theism to resurrection and Christian authority.
The moral objection to specifically Christian redemption and sacrifice.
The claimant's obligation to provide evidence for specifically Christian conclusions.
The earlier move demands a separate evidential route from a possible designer to resurrection and distinctive Christian authority.
The earlier move requires that specifically Christian claims survive historical evidence and rebuttal.
The earlier move objects to the morality of redemption rather than merely the historical occurrence of resurrection.
Whether secular moral feelings and conduct answer the ontological grounding question.
Whether a biological explanation eliminates the need for a distinct normative account.
Whether natural explanation of biological structures resolves moral normativity.
The earlier move uses secular moral behavior to challenge the need for God in morality without resolving the grounding of objective rightness.
The earlier move supplies natural mechanisms as parsimonious explanations within the natural world.
The earlier move cautions that natural and divine deductions can be underdetermined.
Whether secular empathy and sacrifice establish an objective standard rather than merely describe conduct.
Whether moral conduct is possible without divine sanction or belief.
Whether materialism permits responsible and genuinely heroic human action.
The earlier move asks what objectively makes empathy and justice right, beyond describing their biological production.
The earlier move claims objective moral obligation requires a transcendent divine standard.
